title: Nova Pay - Escalation War Room: prep & follow-ups (2026-03-28)
action_items: Maya: coordinate 11:00 war-room and share dial-in + Confluence link by 10:30 2026-03-28
Luis: gather recent request traces and top 50 slow requests (since 03/26) - due 12:00 2026-03-28
Priya: run quick repro on dedicated cluster and test fallback path (model-variant -> smaller quantized) - due 13:30 2026-03-28
Ethan: check autoscaler events and GPU pool utilization for the region (us-west-2) - due 12:30 2026-03-28
Sofia (CS): draft customer update with impact summary and ETA for next update - due 12:45 2026-03-28
content:
Context:
- Nova Pay production (merchant traffic) started seeing intermittent 500s and high tail latency on text-generation endpoints since 2026-03-26 22:00 UTC.
- Impact: checkout timeouts for certain payment flows; reported by Nova Pay SRE with ~5% of sessions affected at peak.
- Customer is on Dedicated tier (reserved capacity) in us-west-2; traffic spike + a model rollout happened 2026-03-26 21:45 (version v3.2.1 -> v3.3.0).

Goals for war-room (11:00 UTC):
1) Stabilize customer traffic (reduce 500s and tail latency).
2) Identify root cause (model, serving runtime, autoscaler, infra).
3) Provide clear customer-facing ETA and next update cadence.
4) Capture action items and owners for 24h remediation plan.

Attendees (invite list):
- Maya Patel (CS lead, owner)
- Luis Martinez (SRE, telemetry & traces)
- Priya Rao (serving-runtime eng, model rollout owner)
- Ethan Brooks (infra / autoscaling)
- Sofia Kim (customer success, comms)
- Optional: Marco Diaz (customer engineering, Nova Pay) - asked to join if available

Pre-meeting notes / quick data to collect before 11:00:
- Latest deploys: confirm canary/rollout status for v3.3.0 (Priya)
- Error types: 500s vs 429s vs timeouts (Luis)
- GPU pool metrics: mem pressure, OOMs, queue lengths, pending pods (Ethan)
- Trace example URLs and top 3 slow endpoints (Luis)
- Any feature flags toggled for Nova Pay traffic (check product console)

Known hypotheses to test (ranked):
A) Model variant v3.3.0 introduced higher memory/latency (most likely given timing).
B) Autoscaler misconfiguration caused delayed scale-up under bursty traffic (plausible).
C) Prefix cache/KV cache invalidation caused repeated compute (possible if rollout changed tokenizer).
D) External upstream (tokenizer service or dependency) had transient errors (less likely but check).

Immediate mitigation options (to discuss & choose):
- Roll back Nova Pay traffic to v3.2.1 (fast, but needs coordination with Priya & infra).
- Route Nova Pay to a fallback model variant (smaller quantized) with compatible output (no schema break).
- Temporarily increase dedicated capacity / bump autoscaler aggressiveness (short-term cost).
- Apply rate-limiting / circuit-breaker on problematic route to reduce customer-visible errors while investigation continues.

Suggested agenda (30-45m):
- 0-5m: quick context & owner confirmations (Maya)
- 5-15m: telemetry review (Luis) - errors, traces, sample requests
- 15-25m: eng analysis (Priya + Ethan) - rollout & infra check, quick repro results
- 25-35m: decide mitigation & assignment (all)
- 35-45m: customer comms draft & next steps (Sofia + Maya)

Notes-to-self / fragile points:
- If rollback chosen, coordinate DB/schema compatibility check (talk to product if needed).
- Watch for hidden failure mode: per-request retries may inflate load - check retry headers.
- Keep customer updates short: impact, what we did, ETA for next update.

Draft customer update (short):
"Nova Pay - quick update: we're investigating increased errors on your checkout inference. Our engineers have scoped likely causes and we are running a targeted mitigation now. Next update in 60 minutes or sooner with ETA to resolution. Apologies for the disruption - Maya (Redwood CS)."

Post-meeting follow-up template (we will paste into Confluence):
- Summary of decision (rollback / route to fallback / scale)
- Timeline of actions taken (with timestamps)
- Root cause (when known) and permanent remediation plan
- Customer-facing post-mortem owner & deadline

Open questions to resolve in war-room:
- Do we have a validated smaller model variant that preserves response schema? (Priya)
- Any ongoing cost/commit constraints that prevent quick capacity bump? (Finance lead via Slack)
- Can Nova Pay temporarily tolerate slightly lower quality for stability? (Marco / product)

Quick links (for meeting):
- Traces dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/nova-pay-traces
- Errors dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/nova-pay-errors
- Incident Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/NOVA-PAY-incident-2026-03-27
- Deploys: https://ci.redwood.ai/pipelines/deploys/serving-runtime

[ ] Run quick repro (Priya)
[ ] Decide mitigation & start implementation
